definition: Machine vision is the technology and methods used to provide imaging-based automatic inspection and analysis for such applications as automatic inspection, process control, and robot guidance, usually in industry.
details: Machine vision refers to many technologies, software and hardware products, integrated systems, actions, methods and expertise. Machine vision as a systems engineering discipline can be considered distinct from computer vision, a form of computer science. It attempts to integrate existing technologies in new ways and apply them to solve real world problems. The term is the prevalent one for these functions in industrial automation environments but is also used for these functions in other environment vehicle guidance. The overall machine vision process includes planning the details of the requirements and project, and then creating a solution. During run-time, the process starts with imaging, followed by automated analysis of the image and extraction of the required information.

explainer.lead: Machine vision covers the technologies and methods that provide imaging-based automatic inspection and analysis for tasks like automatic inspection, process control, and robot guidance, usually in industry. It integrates existing technologies into real-world systems.

tiers.eli5: It's like giving a factory robot a pair of eyes so it can check products as they roll by.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers combine software and hardware products into integrated systems to solve industrial problems; a pitfall is confusing the systems-engineering discipline with computer science research.
tiers.paperLevel: Machine vision is a systems engineering discipline distinct from computer vision, a form of computer science; it integrates existing technologies in new ways rather than developing theory.

explainer.example: An industrial line uses imaging to inspect parts and guide a robot arm.
